title: Green synthesis and characterization of CuO PANI nanocomposite for efficient Pb (II) adsorption from contaminated water

predicted_errors.error_location: Results and discussion, XRD section (paragraph describing g-CuO NPs diffraction peaks)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states the g-CuO NPs show two characteristic peaks at 35° and 38°, 'along with multiple smaller peaks at higher 2θ values (32, 49, 53, 58, 61, and 68°)'. However, 32° is numerically lower than both 35° and 38°, directly contradicting the claim that these additional peaks occur at 'higher 2θ values' than the main peaks.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section, XRD (Figure 1) and FTIR (Figure 2) descriptions
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text introduces Figure 1 as showing 'the XRD graph of the g-CuO NPs, PANI, g-CuO/PANI nanocomposite, and after Pb (II) adsorption' (implying panel order a=CuO, b=PANI), but then states 'The XRD graph of pristine PANI... as shown in Fig. 1a' and 'As shown in Fig. 1b, the XRD pattern of g-CuO nanoparticles...', reversing the stated order. The same reversal occurs for Figure 2: the FTIR intro lists order as 'CuO NPs, PANI, CuO/PANI, and CuO/PANI after Pb (II) adsorption', but the text later assigns 'For PANI... in figure 2 (a)' and 'For g-CuO NPs, as shown in Fig. 2 (b)', again swapping the stated order.

The text states 'the morphology of nanocomposite after Pb (II) adsorption is depicted in Fig. 4 (c)', but a few sentences later, discussing the EDS data for the same after-adsorption sample, states 'the EDS of nanocomposite has Pb in addition to the elements present in CuO/PANI nanocomposite, as shown in Fig. 3 (c)'. Since both statements refer to the same after-adsorption sample characterized via combined SEM/EDX panels (Fig. 3a/b already used for CuO NPs and composite), citing it as both 'Fig. 4(c)' and 'Fig. 3(c)' is an internal contradiction in figure numbering.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section, pH effect on adsorption paragraph
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The pH-effect study states: 'studies were carried out with a pH range of 2 to 6, with initial ion concentration of 25 mg/L, and a CuO/PANI dosage of 25 mg/L.' However, the Materials and Methods section states that 'For the experiments, 100 mL of Pb(II) solutions at varying concentrations were treated with 25 mg of CuO/PANI', which equates to a dosage of 250 mg/L (25 mg / 0.1 L), not 25 mg/L as stated in the pH section — a tenfold discrepancy.

predicted_errors.error_location: Results section, XPS discussion of Pb 4f peaks after adsorption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text first states 'The characteristic peaks of Pb 4f for Pb (II) are observed at 139.25 and 144.14 eV, which are belonged to Pb 4f₇/₂ and Pb 4f₅/₂, respectively'. It then states 'Pb⁴⁺ is responsible for the binding energy peaks at 141.08 eV and 138.43 eV, while Pb (II) is at 138.69 eV and 143.78 eV' — a second, different pair of values (138.69/143.78 eV) is now assigned to 'Pb(II)', contradicting the earlier-stated values (139.25/144.14 eV) for the same oxidation state. Additionally, the claimed Pb⁴⁺ splitting (141.08 − 138.43 = 2.65 eV) is physically inconsistent with the well-established Pb 4f7/2–4f5/2 spin-orbit splitting of ~4.86 eV, and the introduction of Pb⁴⁺ is chemically implausible in a simple aqueous Pb(II) adsorption experiment with no oxidizing agent present.

Before adsorption, the text reports 'Two peaks are also observed for N1s at 399.83 and 401.32 eV' (Fig. S4a). Later, describing the survey scan comparison, it states 'N1s (401.60 eV to 399.83 eV)' shift after adsorption, implying the pre-adsorption N1s value was 401.60 eV — a value that does not match either of the two previously reported pre-adsorption N1s peak positions (399.83 and 401.32 eV).

The text states C1s deconvolution before adsorption gives 'three peaks at 282.75, 286.23, and 290.15 eV' (Fig. S4b). Later, describing the survey scan after adsorption, it states the C1s peak shifted 'from 284.96 eV to 285.04 eV', but neither value (284.96 eV before adsorption) corresponds to any of the three previously reported deconvoluted C1s peak positions.

predicted_errors.error_location: Materials and methods, Synthesis of g-CuO NPs
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The procedure states the CuSO4/plant extract mixture was 'stirred for 60 min at 90 ± 2 ºC at 4000 rpm on a magnetic stirrer.' Standard laboratory magnetic hotplate stirrers typically operate in the range of a few hundred to ~1500-2000 rpm; 4000 rpm is an implausibly high speed for a conventional magnetic stirrer and is not a standard/achievable setting for this type of equipment.
